snippet.title: These 12 Groceries You MUST Stock Up On Before October Ends
snippet.description:
12 Groceries to Stockpile Before Winter | Emergency Food Storage & Survival Pantry Essentials!

Are you prepared for winter storms, extended power outages, and empty grocery store shelves? Discover 12 essential groceries to stockpile before winter that can help keep your family fed when the power goes out, roads close, or supplies become difficult to find.

These affordable emergency food storage essentials include long-lasting pantry staples, survival foods, canned goods, and budget-friendly groceries you can buy at almost any supermarket.

You don't need an expensive emergency food kit or a basement full of survival gear. You need a practical winter emergency pantry stocked with foods that last, provide valuable nutrition, and can be turned into real meals.

And don't miss #1 — one of the cheapest, most versatile long-term food storage staples you can buy!

❄️ IN THIS VIDEO, YOU'LL DISCOVER:

✅ 12 groceries to stockpile before winter storms hit
✅ Best shelf-stable foods for emergency preparedness
✅ Cheap survival foods for a family on a budget
✅ Long-term food storage tips using Mylar bags and food-grade buckets
✅ Foods you can eat without cooking during a blackout
✅ How to build a 2-week emergency food supply
✅ Emergency pantry mistakes to avoid
✅ Why water storage matters as much as food storage
✅ Foods that pair together to create filling survival meals

🛒 THE 12 ESSENTIAL GROCERIES TO STOCKPILE

#12 Peanut Butter – Affordable calories, protein, and healthy fats that require no cooking.

#11 Cooking Oil – Concentrated calories and essential fats for preparing filling meals.

#10 Dry Pasta – Budget-friendly, versatile carbohydrates that cook relatively quickly.

#9 Salt, Sugar & Honey – Long-lasting pantry staples for seasoning, energy, baking, and food preservation.

#8 Canned Vegetables – Shelf-stable nutrition, fiber, and variety when fresh produce isn't available.

#7 Powdered Milk – Convenient protein and calcium without refrigeration before mixing.

#6 Canned Chili, Stew & Soup – Ready-to-eat emergency meals when cooking isn't possible.

#5 Bottled Water – Essential for drinking, food preparation, and basic sanitation.

#4 Rolled Oats – Inexpensive, filling breakfasts that can even be prepared without heat.

#3 Canned Meat & Fish – Shelf-stable complete protein from chicken, tuna, salmon, and other canned meats.

#2 Dried Beans & Lentils – Affordable plant protein, fiber, and long-term pantry nutrition.

#1 White Rice – A low-cost, calorie-dense staple that stores exceptionally well when properly packaged.

🏡 WHY YOU SHOULD STOCKPILE GROCERIES BEFORE WINTER

When a major winter storm approaches, grocery store shelves can empty quickly.

Bread, bottled water, canned goods, and other essentials may become harder to find just when everyone needs them.


🌾 LONG-TERM FOOD STORAGE TIPS

✔ Store dry foods in cool, dry, pest-resistant conditions.
✔ Use suitable food-grade containers and properly sized oxygen absorbers for appropriate dry foods.
✔ Rotate pantry supplies using the first-in, first-out method.
✔ Check expiration and best-by dates regularly.
✔ Keep a manual can opener with your canned foods.
✔ Include foods that require little or no cooking.
✔ Store enough safe drinking water to prepare your emergency meals.

Our goal is simple: Help you prepare before emergencies happen using dependable tools, traditional wisdom, and everyday supplies.

snippet.title: 11 Survival Items the Amish Stockpile at Costco — Before They're Banned
snippet.description:
🔗 The complete Amish Home System — every method from every video, room by room:
https://eliyodersecrets.com

https://youtu.be/WyYz6MmHgT0

On a Saturday morning in a Costco warehouse outside Mount Hope, Ohio, two men in straw hats and plain shirts loaded a flatbed cart with the same eleven items. No organic labels. No brand names. Canning lids. Non-iodized salt. All-purpose flour. Paraffin wax. They do this at the same point every season, the same way their fathers did. The last time Americans paid close attention to what these men were buying, it was 2020, when flat canning lids disappeared from hardware store shelves and sold online for ten dollars a dozen. The Amish families in Holmes County had bought theirs in 2018. This video covers all eleven items — what they are, why now, and what the last one, a ninety-five-cent block from the Costco craft aisle, can do for any house built before 1980 without a permit, a contractor, or a single phone call.

The USDA wheat outlook for the 2026 to 2027 marketing year projects US wheat supplies down eleven percent from the prior year, with winter wheat production at its lowest since 1965 to 1966 and ending stocks down eighteen percent year over year. The USDA sugar and sweeteners outlook for the same period forecasts a tightening supply balance sheet with prices trending upward into spring 2027. A 2008 Department of Energy study confirmed that reflective window barriers in homes built before 1980 reduce summer cooling load by nineteen to twenty-four percent in the rooms where they are installed. A 1979 Pennsylvania State University extension study documented that waxed cotton weatherstripping in pre-1980 homes reduced heating costs by fifteen to twenty-two percent, citing a wartime household conservation manual as its primary reference.

The techniques in this video trace to a 1943 War Department civilian supply document — the Emergency Household Conservation Manual — declassified in 1961 and catalogued at the National Archives. The waxed cotton method for window sealing and pipe insulation appears in that document under civilian heat conservation for homes built before modern weatherstripping. One practitioner in Intercourse, Pennsylvania, wrapped the basement pipes of his 1889 farmhouse with waxed cotton in 1974 after a hard freeze burst the kitchen line. The wraps held fifty years. The Hostetler family ledger from Millersburg, Ohio, recorded bulk commodity prices across sixty-three years from 1956 to 2019: sugar rose six hundred forty percent over that period. Ford truck prices rose nineteen hundred percent. The Amish tracked the difference without a spreadsheet.

This video covers: why non-iodized canning salt is chemically different from table salt and why it matters for every traditional preservation method, the USDA 2026 to 2027 supply projections for wheat and sugar that explain the timing of Amish bulk buying, long-term storage of flour and oats in food-grade buckets with oxygen absorbers, the reflective aluminum foil window barrier from the 2008 DOE study and how to install it this weekend in any pre-1980 home, why strike-anywhere matches are disappearing from American retail and where to find them, the January 1994 ice storm that knocked out power for fourteen days across rural Ohio and Pennsylvania — zero Amish deaths, forty-one among their neighbors — and the full paraffin wax weathercloth technique from the 1943 War Department document: six applications, ninety-five cents per block, no permits required.

• Mixed vegetables (potatoes, carrots, cauliflower, broccoli)
• Pav Bhaji Masala
• Onions
• Ginger garlic
• Butter
• Fresh coriander
• Salt & spices as needed
Pressure cook vegetables with 1 cup water and pav bhaji masala. Mash well. Prepare the masala base with onions and ginger garlic, add vegetables, simmer, and finish with butter and coriander.

🥔 Aloo Tikki
• Boiled potatoes
• Roasted coriander seeds
• Roasted cumin seeds
• Chaat masala
• Black salt
• Cornflour
• Fresh coriander
Mash potatoes and mix with all ingredients. Shape into tikkis, chill for a few hours, then pan fry or air fry until golden and crisp.

🌽 Buttery Corn Pinwheel Bites
• Fresh corn pieces
• Butter
• Chilli flakes
• Roasted cumin powder
• Chilli powder
• Chaat masala
• Black salt
• Fresh coriander

🍮 Kesar Malai Crisp
• Bread slices
• Ghee
• Whipping cream
• Saffron strands
• Badam milk premix (almonds, sugar, saffron & cardamom)
• Chopped nuts
• Rose petals

Fry bread rounds in ghee until golden. Whip cream with saffron and badam premix. Top each crisp bread round with cream and garnish with nuts and rose petals.
